result.title: TVP: TV is Almost All You Need for Speculative Decoding
result.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference with a drafter whose proposed tokens are verified by the target model in parallel. Under lossless speculative sampling, a draft token is accepted with probability one minus the total variation (TV) distance between the target and draft distributions, yet drafters are often trained with cross-entropy (CE) or KL. We first show that under matched and well-tuned training, TV matches or surpasses several published draft-training objectives when fine-tuning, and a fixed TV and KL mixture does the same when training from scratch. We identify two remaining problems, TV's vanishing gradients on undercovered tokens and the prefix products that starve later positions in acceptance-length objectives. To address both, we derive TVP, a loss family based on expected acceptance length, whose power parameter interpolates between coverage and acceptance oriented objectives. Annealing the power from zero to one gives the highest or tied-highest acceptance length across three drafter architectures and three target models, including longer drafts and block verification. TVP improves acceptance length over CE by 9.8% when fine-tuning, and over the public DFlash2 training recipes by 6.2 to 12.9%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究投机解码中草稿模型的训练目标：指出无损投机采样下接受概率为 1 减去目标与草稿分布的 TV 距离，据此提出基于期望接受长度的损失族 TVP，用幂参数在覆盖与接受导向目标间插值并退火，在多种草稿架构与目标模型上取得更高接受长度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「草稿—验证接受概率」表述与期望接受长度训练目标，可供核查是否能迁移到 latent 推理中的多步草稿生成、验证与计算分配；但工作本身围绕 token 级解码加速，与视觉推理状态无直接联系。
